title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results from the last run, decide on model variant to pin for the next week, discuss rollback/fallback strategy, and agree next steps to run canary traffic and share security docs. Customer is leaning toward Redwood-hosted with dedicated fallback to a smaller quantized variant; latency vs cost tradeoffs and KV cache behavior were key discussion points.

Customer to confirm target SLOs and traffic profile for canary (James) - ETA 2026-07-03
Schedule canary run for pinned model (Priya/Alex to coordinate) - tentative 2026-07-07
Redwood to send SOC2/ISO summary and network topology notes (Priya) - ETA 2026-07-02

Priya Patel - Prepare canary run plan and test script (latency + QPS) - due 2026-07-06

transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-06-30 10:00 UTC · 45 min
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), James Lee (BrightRetail ML Lead), Sara Gomez (BrightRetail Eng Manager), Michael Park (BrightRetail CTO)

Summary: quick recap then deep dive into the latest benchmark run (overnight) and decision on which model to pin for the pilot. Talked through fallback/rollback rules and what to do if latency or quality regressions appear.

00:00 Alex Morgan: okay everybody thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, quick agenda review — benchmark results, model pinning recommendation, rollback/fallback strategy, next steps
00:18 James Lee: thanks alex. quick thing, we ran the batch across our 10k sample overnight, getting curious about latency tail and token cost so excited to see the numbers
00:32 Priya Patel: hey team, i pulled the spreadsheet into the shared drive, the important columns are p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, and cost per 1k tokens. note that the overnight run used their prod-like prompt set with longer completion lengths
00:48 Sara Gomez: real quick, can you remind us which variants were included? i saw the catalog names but some of them look similar
01:02 Priya Patel: sure, we tested three main variants: redwood-open-l7-1.2 (full float), redwood-open-l7-1.2-quant (8-bit quantized), and redwood-lite-l7-1.0 (smaller model). also tried a warm cache versus cold cache slice to show KV prefix benefits
01:26 Michael Park: any surprises on quality when quantized? we can't accept hallucinations for product descriptions
01:39 Priya Patel: good q — on our evals the 8-bit quantized version had a tiny drop on BLEU/ROUGE and our custom quality rubric, about 2-3% lower on certain categories (formatting), but overall semantic correctness stayed high. we flagged the prompt templates that needed small tweaks
02:05 Alex Morgan: looking at the latency table, p95 for full float was around 420ms, quant was 330ms, and the lite model was 210ms. cost per 1M tokens: float ~$120, quant ~$85, lite ~$40 — these are host pricing estimates for the test config
02:28 James Lee: p99s? that's the one that worries us for interactive UI latency
02:34 Priya Patel: p99 float ~1.1s, quant ~0.85s, lite ~0.6s. but important note: with prefix caching enabled the p99 for repeat prompts dropped by ~30-40% for all variants
02:52 Sara Gomez: that cache note is big. our UI has a lot of repeated product description patterns so we might see outsized gains. how does that affect pinning decision?
03:08 Alex Morgan: suggests a hybrid approach — pin to redwood-open-l7-1.2-quant for general traffic for balance of quality and cost, but route a small percentage to redwood-lite-l7-1.0 as a cheaper fallback for bulk throughput or when latency spikes. keep redwood-open-l7-1.2 float as an emergency rollback if quality metrics dip below threshold
03:34 Michael Park: ok that makes sense. can we do automatic fallback by latency threshold and also quality-triggered rollback? meaning if latency > 900ms for sustained window then fallback to lite, and if quality score drops below 90% on eval set then rollback to float
03:52 Priya Patel: yes the routing layer supports policy rules: latency-based routing, and quality monitoring can trigger a manual or automated rollback. for automated quality rollback we usually recommend a canary with active evals — if canary quality drops we flip back automatically but teams usually want a human confirmation for rollback to float for safety
04:20 James Lee: what's the risk with automated rollback flipping to float? is float more expensive so we'd blow budget if false positive?
04:31 Alex Morgan: correct, float is costlier. we can add budget guardrails — e.g., max % of traffic to float for rollback or require approval after x hours. also can pair rollback with rate-limited traffic to control spend during the recovery window
04:50 Sara Gomez: regarding pinning, how do we express the pin config? is it catalog_name:version string? we need to paste into our infra repo
05:02 Priya Patel: yes it's a simple config: model_catalog_name=redwood-open-l7, pinned_version=1.2-quant, fallback=[redwood-lite-l7:1.0], rollback_policy={metric:quality, threshold:0.9, action:rollback_to:float:1.2}. i'll send a snippet, it's straightforward to integrate with your feature flagging service
05:34 James Lee: can you make sure the model names are consistent with the catalog? last time we saw a mismatch because of slight naming differences between the UI and the API
05:44 Alex Morgan: good call — we'll include canonical catalog names with exact variants and model IDs in the spreadsheet and in the pinning config.
05:55 Michael Park: quick security question — for the dedicated fallback we may want traffic to stay inside our VPC for some data classes. can Redwood do per-route VPC pinning?
06:09 Priya Patel: yes for private deployments, routing by route is supported. for hosted we can do customer-specific routing rules but if you need full VPC isolation that's usually Dedicated or Private deployment. we also provide KMS integrations and audit logs for each request
06:30 Sara Gomez: perfect. also want to confirm data retention for logs tied to canary — we need 30-day retention for debugging then purge
06:40 Alex Morgan: we'll include retention options in the security doc we send — you can set retention windows per-log stream
06:50 James Lee: on the latency tests, did the overnight run use dynamic batching? our traffic is spiky so batching may not help much at low QPS
07:02 Priya Patel: tests ran with continuous batching enabled with a small batching window to emulate burst traffic. we can run an additional test that disables batching to see cold QPS performance; that might be more representative for your low-latency UI calls
07:20 Alex Morgan: action item — run a cold QPS test (no batching) and a second warm cache run to quantify delta. we'll report p50/p95/p99 and costs.
07:33 Michael Park: how about model quantization compatibility with our evaluation pipelines? we need deterministic outputs for A/B evals
07:44 Priya Patel: quantized outputs are slightly different but deterministic given same seeds and environment. for A/B, we'd recommend running paired evaluations side-by-side and using our eval harness; we'll attach the eval scripts to the spreadsheet
08:05 James Lee: what about rollbacks and model state — does the KV cache get wiped on rollback? we don't want stale cached prefixes served to users after a rollback
08:18 Priya Patel: rolling back the model doesn't automatically flush customer caches. we recommend a coordinated cache invalidation step in the rollback plan; Redwood's runtime can also mark cache entries as versioned so they are ignored when the model changes if you enable that mode
08:40 Sara Gomez: ok that's helpful. network wise we'll need an IP allowlist for testing; i'll send the list to priya after this call
08:50 Alex Morgan: noted — sara please send allowlist; priya will confirm ports and test endpoints
09:00 Priya Patel: small note on metrics: we'll expose per-route cost and latency metrics, plus per-model quality evals; you can wire them into your datadog or looker dashboards
09:14 James Lee: good. any blockers from redwood side to start the canary next week?
09:21 Alex Morgan: none, we just need the traffic slice and SLOs from you, and we'll finalize the pinning config. also need confirmation if you want automated rollback or manual approval on quality triggers
09:35 James Lee: let's go manual for initial canary, automated later once we trust the metrics
09:43 Sara Gomez: agreed. and can we keep a 5% traffic to the lite fallback during the canary just to see behavior in production?
09:52 Priya Patel: yes can do — route 95% to pinned quant, 5% to lite fallback, and keep float as cold backup at 0% unless manual rollback is triggered
10:05 Michael Park: any estimated cost impact for keeping 5% on lite? minimal, should be cheaper overall
10:10 Alex Morgan: we'll include a delta calc in the spreadsheet for the canary mix
10:18 James Lee: last thing, comp vendors mentioned — we evaluated openai chat endpoints and anthopic models, bedrock looked promising but integration complexity was higher. your hosting perf was better on tail latency in our tests
10:34 Alex Morgan: thanks for that context. we'll include the competitor notes in the benchmark doc for completeness
10:42 Alex Morgan: ok quick recap of next steps and owners, then we'll adjourn
10:50 Priya Patel: recap: alex shares spreadsheet, priya prepares canary plan and test scripts, james provides traffic slice and SLOs, sara sends IP allowlist and eng contacts. everyone aims to have items done early next week so we can run canary on 7/7.
10:55 James Lee: sounds good, thanks everyone
10:58 Alex Morgan: thank you all, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed pin config
11:00 Meeting end
